build_note: Installed from the pinned pure-Python py3-none-any wheel by hash; the image checks that the wheel's namespy/ package is byte-identical to the pinned sdist, that the wheel declares only optional (extra) requirements, and that packet.py, wire.py, names.py, rdata.py and the LICENSE match recorded SHA-256 values. No runtime dependencies.
dependencies_note: atheris 3.1.0 is the in-process fuzz bridge only; namespy 0.1.0 has no runtime dependencies (its crypto, doh and dev extras are not installed).
parser_family: namespy (packet.py DnsPacket/DnsRecord over wire.py, names.py DomainName decompression and rdata.py per-type RData classes)
api: namespy.DnsPacket.parse(local DNS message bytes) -> (DnsPacket, octets consumed)
coverage: Python line tracing of the installed namespy package during valid-control replay; Atheris import instrumentation for the byte-input bridge
scope: One RFC 1035 DNS message from local bytes via namespy.DnsPacket.parse (strict mode): header flags (the reserved Z bit, AD and CD are separate library fields joined into z), questions, and CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers with compressed names; valid response and query controls only. RDATA text is the library's RData.to_presentation(); the harness only lower-cases names and checks the trailing dot. Importing namespy imports the socket module, but an instrumented run of both controls created no socket and opened no file; the resolver, server and DoH modules are never started.
